dimensions.completeness: Are all relevant test scope dimensions covered?
dimensions.specificity: Are test descriptions concrete and actionable?
dimensions.risk_calibration: Is the coverage depth (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) appropriate? R=5 correct+good justification, R=4 correct+weak justification, R=3 one level off, R=1-2 two levels off
dimensions.integration_awareness: Does the recommendation identify relevant cross-system touchpoints?
dimensions.clarification_flag_quality: Are flagged gaps genuinely useful and materially relevant?

rubric_description.type: BASELINE — naive prompt, no ATSR framework

scores.notes: Main test areas covered but regression thin. Functional tests OK, but smoke/regression descriptions generic. Coverage HIGH vs MEDIUM — one level off. Integration identifies POS-to-portal sync but descriptions generic. Flags not specific or actionable.

Reconnection scenario covered and matrix partially named, but HIGH vs LOW is two levels off — a vendor firmware patch fix is clearly LOW depth. Integration generic. Flags irrelevant (security checks not applicable to a reconnection fix).
4 network types covered, regression on POS communication present but thin. Test descriptions mostly generic connectivity checks. HIGH vs MEDIUM — one level off. Integration and flags generic.

Main areas covered but doesn't enumerate the 9 specific report types. Regression very generic ('ensure existing POS functionalities are unaffected'). Depth correct. Integration identifies BI platform but not specific. Loyalty flag is actually out of scope per spec.

Names 2x medium pricing, modifier count of 6, 3 beverage categories — good specificity. But MEDIUM vs HIGH is one level off for a new size tier addition with new pricing logic. Integration generic. Flags generic.

Covers date/time separation and edge cases, names specific config fields. HIGH vs MEDIUM — one level off for an enhancement. Integration generic. Flags relevant (end date before start date is a valid edge case).

Lists roles for both brands and covers legitimate operations — strong completeness. Depth HIGH vs MEDIUM — one level off for an access control config change. Integration generic. First flag irrelevant (no regional exceptions mentioned); second flag about food item replication is in the spec.

Covers main areas but misses multi-environment progression (UAT/Pre-Prod/Prod). MEDIUM vs LOW — one level off for a config value change. Flags are excellent: retroactivity and third-party coordination both match the key open questions in the ground truth.
Main areas covered but misses multi-environment progression. MEDIUM vs LOW — one level off for cert rotation. Test descriptions somewhat generic. Vendor confirmation flag is relevant.
Core scenarios covered but regression thin. Depth correct. Mobile app to POS and pricing engine integration specifically identified. Flags generic.
Names specific sections (Tender Media, Group Sales, Discounts, Service Charges). Depth correct. Integration tests generic ('data source' and 'export formats'). Flags not specific.
Zone assignment and page design covered, explicitly excludes limited-menu designs. Depth correct. Integration generic. Flags not specific.

Strong: covers all 4 device/OS combinations explicitly. MEDIUM vs HIGH — one level off for a platform version upgrade. Pending release notes flag is excellent and critical. Integration generic ('backend services').

Names 'CANCEL TRANSACTION' message text verbatim — excellent specificity. But completeness thin: regression is shallow, integration not explored. MEDIUM vs LOW — one level off for a UI bug fix. Flags partially relevant.
Same core failure as ATSR: does not identify BIN range boundary/conflict testing as the primary objective. Regression tests generic. HIGH vs MEDIUM — one level off. Flags moderately relevant.
Names Windows Defender, remote tunneling tool, core POS operations. Depth correct. Integration mentions different Windows Defender versions but generic. Flags relevant but not highly actionable.

Covers creation, display, regression, some edge cases. MEDIUM vs HIGH — one level off for a new feature. Integration identifies clock-in trigger but generic. Flags relevant (character count, priority) but miss the architectural unknowns that ATSR surfaced.

Comprehensive list of all system areas from the spec. Depth correct. But specificity is poor — all 14 functional tests follow 'Verify DNS resolution for X' pattern with no scenario detail. Integration and flags are solid.

depth_calibration_accuracy.note: Baseline over-assigns HIGH — 9 of 18 specs assigned HIGH vs 6 in ground truth. Without calibration rules, the model defaults to treating most enterprise changes as high-risk.
